text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.

GERMANY - German Bunds were steady in late trade, turning their attention from what turned out to be uneventful U.S. producer price data to consumer price figures due on tomorrow. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.64, down 0.07 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilt futures closed down after a higher than expected decline in October's unemployment figures, trading remained subdued as markets were cautious ahead of Thursday's October RPI data and flood of U.S. data. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 108-27/32, down 23/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures settled little changed after calm session with traders and analysts waiting for some more solid signals from the United States to shake the market out of its current range. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 127.44, up 0.04 from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and futures ended firm but off session highs in a market awaiting news on the fate of the country's key 1997 budget. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 126.58, up 0.30 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury prices opened slightly higher ahead of the U.S. October report on wholesale prices and a Federal Reserve policy meeting, two events investors believe will be benign for the bond market. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 114-14/32, down 15/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.48 percent.

JAPAN - The key December Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended Tokyo session sharply higher, as it continued to attract bids after the recent sell-off. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 124.58, up 0.38 from Tuesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The Eurobond market saw an sudden surge in new issue activity after several more lethargic days, a handful of retail-targeted dollar bonds surfaced. General Motor Acceptance Corp issued a $200 million bond maturing in January 2001 at 32 basis points over U.S. Treasuries and Landesbank Schleswig-Holstein a $200 million issue due in June 2000 at 10 b.p. over.
